To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best interpolation results of the return period of extreme values of FFDI were obtained by using a random forest and inverse weighting distance interpolation algorithms.
the return period of extreme FFDI is higher during the summer months in southern Australia and in spring in northern Australia.

the spatial distribution of FFDI return periods shows that the highest values are found in the interior of the continent during spring and summer and the highest values occur in the eastern states of Australia during spring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial distribution of fire weather danger indices and the extreme values of fire danger.
developing an accurate spatial distribution of the FFDI return periods across Australia.
the development of spatially distributed fire danger index for the entire country.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fire danger in Australia is higher in the inland than in the coast and in the north than in the south.

the FFDIs are higher in the interior of Australia, particularly in the eastern half of the country, than in the coastal regions and that the highest fire weather conditions occur in spring in northern Australia and in summer in southern Australia.
the FFDIs are higher in inland areas of Australia than coastal areas and higher during spring and summer than other seasons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the spatial interpolation of the return period of the McArthur's Forest Danger Index can provide valuable information to assess the spatial distribution of severe fire weather conditions across Australia.
the use of machine learning techniques for interpolating the spatial distribution of fire danger indices provides more accurate results than the use of conventional methods.
the spatial distribution of extreme values of fire weather danger indices can be estimated with reasonable accuracy using the proposed methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial distribution of extreme fire danger index can be obtained by applying machine learning methods to the existing network of weather recording stations.
the spatial distribution of fire danger conditions in a large country like Australia can be assessed using the spatial interpolation algorithms presented in this study.
the spatial distribution of FFDI can help fire management agencies in their planning of fire management strategies.
